checks.finding: requirements.md AC-010 states TEST-019 (tests/loop-escalation.tests.sh) asserts the quality-gate-outcome/capability-applicability event kind 'a Context-present round drive produces' — explicitly scoping this assertion to the Context-present fixture state, the same class of claim that every other genuinely Context-present-scoped AC in this package (AC-007, AC-019-AC-021, AC-042, AC-043) pairs with an explicit 'named SKIP entry in REQ-007's allowlist manifest ... until Epic A1 merges' clause, because Context-present machinery does not exist until Epic A1 lands (INV-013, INV-017). AC-010 carries no such SKIP clause, and acceptance-tests.md's AC-010/TEST-010 row Test Type column ('integration') carries no '(named SKIP ...)' annotation, unlike the Test Type cells for AC-004/AC-007/AC-019-021/AC-036/AC-037/AC-042/AC-043 which all do. Separately, INV-014 and the Field Definitions section establish that 'disabled-legacy' is definitionally the Context-absent state, and AC-009 makes the capability_applicability field (disabled-legacy/advisory/required) an addition this epic's own Phase 2/3 work populates without needing Epic A1 — meaning the observation TEST-019 could in principle be exercised today via the disabled-legacy value, in tension with AC-010's own 'Context-present' wording. Two implementers would reasonably diverge: one would gate TEST-019's capability-applicability assertion behind an Epic A1 SKIP (matching the sibling-AC pattern for every other Context-present claim), another would build it as an unconditional, always-run assertion (matching the absence of any SKIP tag in acceptance-tests.md and AC-025's untagged text). This is a specification-level ambiguity, not an implementation-architecture question, and belongs to spec review because it concerns which fixture state a required, already-numbered test case (TEST-019) must assert against and whether it is gated at all — a decision the package must fix, not leave to be guessed downstream. Major because it risks a divergent SKIP-vs-ASSERT implementation choice for a named, already-numbered test case, not a specification-blocking contradiction.

The Overview's dated amendment note explicitly flags that its own 'Phase 1 only, no later-phase artifacts' framing and the Non-goals' Phase 2/3 deferral describe authoring-time state only, and points to investigation.md's `## Amendment Re-Review Context` as the current, authoritative framing. That section conforms to the calibration's full evidence bar: three full (40-hex-char) amendment commit hashes; SHA-256 values for requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md at each amendment commit that match this manifest's own pinned hashes for both files (b302af8d...02811 and d982efe1...09d04 respectively, confirming internal consistency rather than a bare assertion); two verbatim, dated (2026-08-23) human-approval quotations; and commit/SHA-256 citations for every later-phase artifact referenced (tasks.md, traceability.md/.json, design.md, tests/loop-inventory.tests.sh/.ps1, tests/lib/loop-driver.sh/.ps1). Per the calibration's Amendment Re-Review Context rule, this suppresses the phase-sequencing finding basis that would otherwise apply to the Non-goals/Overview vs. later-phase-artifact tension; no other direct, non-phase-sequencing conflict between a requirement, acceptance criterion, constraint, or non-goal was found within the reviewed artifacts (e.g. AC-025's 'always the last quality-gate-outcome event when both fire' and AC-026's 'always last in a round's own event sub-sequence' were checked and found compatible — the former scopes only the two quality-gate-outcome producers' relative order, the latter scopes done-transition's position among all event kinds).

acceptance-tests.md pairs material negative/boundary paths with explicit ACs: AC-002 (byte-identical negative self-check against a deliberately mutated fixture), AC-035 (three independent negative self-checks — dependency-present SKIP, unknown SKIP, fingerprint drift), AC-041 (two independent negative fixtures for promote-golden-baseline.sh's CI-set and missing/empty --approved-by refusal paths, asserting non-zero exit and no file write), and AC-033's golden negative test for the capability-only emit-run-record.sh flag combination (usage error, no $out file). The three Edge Cases requirements.md names (Context-present-invalid distinguishability, non-silent baseline pinning to a fixed commit, and per-entry-partial capability-field extension being valid) are each traced to AC-019-AC-021/AC-018, respectively, or are explicitly framed as a documented, non-testable permissive statement (partial per-entry extension).

requirements.md's Assumptions section names three assumptions (upstream epic instability for A1/A3/A4/A5/A6; decision-doc/ADR authority; jq/bash/PowerShell runtime). The first, highest-risk assumption is not left as a bare unresolved caveat: it is explicitly tied to REQ-007's fingerprint-drift hard-fail mechanism (AC-035c) as its mitigation, and the Assumptions text itself states this package 're-verifies before Phase 2/3 begins, per investigation.md's Safety constraints.' All three Open Questions (OQ-001, OQ-002, OQ-003) are marked '(resolved)' with the decision and its rationale recorded in-line, leaving no assumption or open question that is neither resolved nor explicitly flagged as a decision needed before design/task decomposition.

The package specifies an irreversible-change/governance boundary — promotion of a golden-baseline candidate to canonical — and makes it testable rather than aspirational: Roles and Permissions and Security Boundaries B1 fix that only a human 'Maintainer' (a defined role) approves a candidate->canonical promotion PR; REQ-006c/AC-018 fix the two-stage candidate/canonical procedure; AC-040 is a static CI-workflow-text scan hard-failing if `promote-golden-baseline.sh`/`--write-candidate` appear in `.github/workflows/test.yml`; and AC-041 exercises the script's own runtime refusal directly with two independent negative fixtures (CI env var set; --approved-by omitted/empty), each asserting non-zero exit and no write to the canonical path.

The same AC-010/TEST-019 gap identified under AMBIGUITY (requirements.md AC-010's 'a Context-present round drive produces' framing vs. acceptance-tests.md's AC-010/TEST-010 row carrying no upstream-dependency SKIP annotation, unlike every sibling Context-present-scoped AC) means a design/implementation-policy reviewer inheriting this package cannot determine, from the specification alone, whether TEST-019's capability-applicability assertion is gated behind Epic A1 merging or is meant to run unconditionally against the disabled-legacy value. Because REQ-007/AC-034's allowlist-manifest mechanism and the SKIP-vs-ASSERT disposition are exactly the kind of product behavior this package elsewhere fixes explicitly and exhaustively for every other upstream-dependent assertion (AC-028's disposition legend, AC-034's allowlist), leaving this one instance unresolved requires the downstream reviewer to invent the missing disposition rather than being handed a closed decision, which is the specific readiness failure this check is scoped to catch.

No `domain/` directory exists at the repository root (confirmed via directory listing), so the applicability precondition (a `domain/context-map.md` recording `Domain-Model-Status: Approved` and a schema-valid `domain/domain-contract.json`) is not met. Recorded as skipped per the check's explicit skip condition.
